notes:
Summary: Large developer org (platform & apps teams) evaluating Redwood to power IDE copilot across ~1,200 engineers. Primary concerns: runaway token cost from long-context copilot sessions, consistent low-latency streaming in IDE, and ability to pin model versions per team. Interested in experiment: Dedicated GPU pool with automatic prefix/KV caching, mixed-precision quantization profiles to hit token-cost targets, and per-seat cost projection. SE asked about realistic cache hit rates (expected 30-45% for shared snippets) and rollback strategy if quantization reduces code suggestion quality.

Quoted from CTO: 'We need predictable per-seat economics — our finance team won't accept open-ended token bills.'

POC scope notes (from AE): 1) set up Dedicated cluster in our VPC for two teams, 2) run 10k streaming completion sessions with telemetry, 3) evaluate Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization, 4) measure dev-perceived latency at 95th pctile.

Billing ask: want a proposal that maps to per-seat steady-state target ($10-15/mo per active developer) or a committed GPU seat model.

Security: must demonstrate KMS integration + audit log retention 1 year. Compliance team flagged data residency for HR-related repos.
